subject: [PATCH] mm: mempolicy: fix automatic numa balancing for shmem

reviews.author: Huang, Ying
reviews.summary: Reviewer Huang questioned the correctness of using the task's mempolicy for kernel allocations, considering scenarios where pages are used privately or shared, and requested a solution to address this issue.
reviews.raw_body:
What is the right mempolicy for these random kernel allocations?  If the
pages are used privately by the task (not the case in your example, but
is it possible?), is it OK to use the mempolicy of the task?  If the
pages are shared, what is the correct mempolicy?  Will it be fixed?  Or
can we find a way to change the policy?

[snip]

---
Best Regards,
Huang, Ying

reviews.author: Gregory Price
reviews.summary: Reviewer Gregory Price noted that the patch's allocations should use the system default (local node) instead of the task policy, and suggested dropping the first commit to ship only the second one.
reviews.raw_body:
I submitted a recommendation[1], but I think it got swalled by the kvack
outage, i'll probably need to re-send.

At the very least, these allocations should just use the system default
(local node) instead of the task.

I left the page-cache affected by this (so inode data DOES follow this)
but after some testing I found this amounts to around ~0.4% of total
memory usage when you have many small files (~64kb files, 512GB cached).

I think we can probably drop the first commit and just ship the second.

The fun result - when you combine this fix + private nodes [2] you can
reliably hotplug a private node in ZONE_NORMAL so long as all tasks that
were using the private node were reaped prior to hotplug.

This is a legitimately useful improvement in my opinion.

~Gregory

[1] https://lore.kernel.org/all/20260701222112.2820098-1-gourry@gourry.net/
[2] https://lore.kernel.org/all/20260222084842.1824063-1-gourry@gourry.net/

2026-07-06.patch_summary: This patch fixes a problem where mapped shared memory (shmem) was not considered for NUMA balancing on tiered systems. The issue arose from a previous commit that intended to limit NUMA scanning to migrate-on-fault VMAs, but incorrectly treated the absence of a shared policy as an explicit opt-out. The patch changes the vma_policy_mof function to use __get_vma_policy directly, allowing default policy VMAs to participate in balancing while still excluding explicitly pinned memory. This fix should improve performance on tiered systems with cachelib-based workloads.
